standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, the lemma that the normalization of a Nagata scheme is finite, and More on Morphisms, the lemma that the category of projective schemes is stable under composition
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction to a normal projective modification and the unique point above the chosen point with the same local ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent of modifications along a localization and vanishing of the first cohomology
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Limits, the lemmas spreading a modification of the local ring to a modification of the projective scheme and checking properness, and Same chapter, the exact sequence used to conclude the vanishing of the first direct image

core_obligations: Realize the extension (proof lines 2043-2058): present B as a localization of a finite type algebra over A whose image in B is a domain with the same fraction field, embed its spectrum in an affine space over A and take the closure in projective space; the dimension formula and the algebraicity of residue field extensions show that the chosen point is closed, so B is the local ring of a projective modification at a closed point.

Reduce to a normal projective modification (proof lines 2058-2066): since A is Nagata the normalization of the modification is finite, hence the normalized modification is still projective over A; as B is normal its local ring equals the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the normalization at the point, so there is a unique point above it with the same local ring, and one may assume the modification is normal.

Transfer the vanishing (proof lines 2066-2082): for a modification of the spectrum of B with normal source the spreading lemma provides a morphism of the projective scheme which is an isomorphism away from the point and restricts to the given modification there; the local rings of this scheme are either local rings of the original modification or of the given one, so it is normal, and its first cohomology vanishes by the rationality assumption on A; the exact sequence then gives that the first direct image of the structure sheaf under the spreading morphism vanishes, which is exactly the vanishing required for B to define a rational singularity.
proof_roadmap: Present the extension as a local ring of a projective modification at a closed point.
Pass to the normalization and reduce to a normal projective modification with the same local ring at the chosen point.
Spread a modification of that local ring to the projective scheme, use normality and the rationality assumption to get the vanishing, and read it back via the exact sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if a local normal Nagata domain of dimension two defines a rational singularity, then so does any normal local extension of dimension two with the same fraction field which is essentially of finite type (statement lines 2034-2041). The proof (proof lines 2043-2084) realizes the extension as a local ring of a projective modification at a closed point, reduces to a normal projective modification, spreads modifications of the local ring back to the projective scheme, and transfers the cohomological vanishing through the exact sequence. H3: a multi-step reduction with a spreading argument, written out in full.
